<reflection>
The first experiment provided initial kinetic data, but the negative log-likelihood values for most mechanisms are extremely close (within ~2 units), indicating that the data from a single moderate-condition experiment is insufficient to discriminate among the majority of mechanisms. Only M5 is clearly ruled out (positive NLL), while M3, M4, and M5 are less likely but not definitively excluded. The aim of the first turn was achieved by obtaining baseline data, but substantial uncertainty remains across many mechanisms.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To discriminate among the many plausible mechanisms, we need an experiment that amplifies differences in their predicted behaviors. A key distinction among mechanisms is their dependence on catalyst concentration. Mechanisms involving dimerization (M2, M3, M19), catalyst activation (M6, M8), or deactivation (M9, M14, M20) will exhibit non-linear scaling of initial rate with catalyst concentration, whereas simple Michaelis-Menten (M1) predicts linear scaling. By reducing catalyst concentration by a factor of 20 (from 0.02 to 0.001 M) while keeping substrate concentration constant (2.0 M), we probe the low-catalyst regime where non-linear effects become more pronounced relative to the linear baseline. This condition avoids extreme saturation or depletion, maintains the same substrate context as run 1 for direct comparison, and should generate distinct kinetic profiles across mechanisms with different catalyst orders.
</hypothesis>
